questions.reason: Floyd–Warshall builds all-pairs distances by allowing one more intermediate vertex k at each stage. It takes the minimum of the previous distance i→j and the previous distances i→k plus k→j.
questions.note: The Made Easy table agrees with A. Its explanation names Bellman–Ford, whose standard formulation is single-source. Floyd–Warshall is the direct all-pairs dynamic program.

questions.reason: A k-bit target can be 2^k−1, so filling the n-by-(W+1) table takes pseudopolynomial time in binary input length. Unary input length includes W. Subset sum is in NP by certificate verification and is weakly NP-complete.
questions.note: Made Easy keys D. D is true when read as printed in the original 2008 paper, “The subset sum problem is NP-hard,” which also corrects the app’s “in NP-hard” typo. B is the intended false statement for the usual Θ(nW) dynamic program. The question states O(nW), an upper bound. No matching question was found in the three GATE Overflow PDFs.

questions.reason: Each value L_i uses the solved subproblem L_{i+1} when adjacent elements increase. A right-to-left pass followed by a maximum scan takes linear time.
questions.note: The recurrence computes the longest contiguous strictly increasing run. Evaluate i from n−2 down to 0 and return max(L_0, L_1, …, L_{n−1}). The app’s L_{n+1} is outside the defined array of lengths.
